name: "Freezer Friendly" Classic Beef Chili with Mixed Beans, Bell Pepper & Onion (Batch-Cooking)

instructions.primary_message: Wash, dry, trim, and medium dice bell peppers. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 green bell pepper
1 orange bell pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.

Once the pot is hot, working in batches, add beef, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 5-6 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl. (Discard all but 2 tablespoons drippings from the pot, then reserve pot for later use.)
instructions.secondary_message:
3 lb lean ground beef
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, peel, halve, and small dice onions; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the bell pepper.
When the beef is done, return the reserved pot (with 2 tbsp drippings) to medium-high heat. Add veggies to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6-7 minutes.
While the veggies are cooking, drain and rinse beans. Set aside to drain further.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (15 oz) can pinto beans
1 (15 oz) can kidney beans

instructions.primary_message: When the veggies are softened, add tomato paste to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tomato paste darkens in color, about 5 minutes.

Return beef (and any accumulated juices) to the pot along with drained beans, tomatoes, 3 cups broth, and spices; stir to combine the chili and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat and simmer until chili is thickened, 35-45 minutes (if desired, add up to 1 cup additional broth, as needed, for a looser chili). Remove from heat, add vinegar, and stir to combine. Let cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally, about 30 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (14.5 oz) can fire-roasted diced tomatoes
4 cups beef broth
¼ cup chili powder
2 tbsp cumin, ground
2 tsp oregano, dried
1 ½ tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper
½ tsp cayenne pepper
2 tbsp apple cider vinegar

instructions.primary_message: Once the chili has cooled to room temperature, divide between containers.

STORING: Cover each container with an air-tight lid (or wrap tightly with plastic wrap). Place in the freezer for up to 3 months. HEATING: For best results, thaw chili in the fridge overnight. Warm in a saucepan set over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until heated through, 6-8 minutes.

CHEF'S NOTE: Serve chili with your choice of toppings such as sour cream (or plain Greek yogurt), shredded Cheddar cheese, sliced green onions, chopped cilantro, pickled jalapeños, diced avocado, or tortilla chips. Enjoy!
